open_points.subject: A1 — conflict-copy classification versus R0-12
open_points.text:
A name is ignored, in any letter case and at every level of the path, when it begins with a dot or
with `~syncthing~`, ends in `.tmp` or `~`, or contains `.sync-conflict-`, the mark of a Syncthing
conflict copy (R0-14).

A scan covers the photo folder and all its subfolders. Subfolders carry no meaning for the Portal.
open_points.question: Is every name containing `.sync-conflict-` ignored, including an ordinary user-named file, or is the exception limited to files actually created by Syncthing as conflict copies?
options: Ignore only a verified Syncthing conflict copy; offer an ordinary matching file.
Declare that every matching name is treated as a conflict copy regardless of origin.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the filename marker as the complete definition and ignore every matching name.

witness.initial: The photo folder contains an ordinary JPEG named `holiday.sync-conflict-notes.jpg`; Syncthing did not create it.
events: The owner asks the calling flow to scan the photo folder.
outcomes: R0-12 makes the ordinary file available for delivery because everything under the photo folder is delivered on choice.
A1 ignores the file because its name contains `.sync-conflict-`.
witness.observer: The owner, who either sees or does not see the photo in the scan.

open_points.subject: A1 — placement identity for conflict copies
open_points.text: INV-18: a conflict copy, in the folder or a subfolder and in either letter case, is absent from the scan and placing it by its hash fails with `not_ready_or_absent` (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`).
open_points.question: What happens when the same source hash belongs both to an ignored conflict-copy path and to a non-ignored ordinary path, given that the placement request identifies content by the hash rather than identifying a path?
options: Placement succeeds because a non-ignored file with that hash exists.
Placement fails because any conflict-copy path with that hash poisons the hash.
The operation must receive an additional path or scan-observation identity.
open_points.default_guess: Succeed when at least one non-ignored regular file with the requested hash is eligible.

witness.initial: `photo.jpg` and `photo.sync-conflict-20261118-device.jpg` contain identical bytes and therefore have the same source hash; the first is ordinary and the second is ignored.
events: The calling flow scans the folder and receives the ordinary file with hash H.
The calling flow requests placement by H.
outcomes: The ordinary file is eligible, so placement of H succeeds.
The request is described as placing the conflict copy by its hash, so it fails with `not_ready_or_absent`.
witness.observer: The calling flow receives either a placement or a refusal.

open_points.subject: A1 and M04 — conflict exclusion versus idempotent replay
open_points.text:
INV-18: a conflict copy, in the folder or a subfolder and in either letter case, is absent from the scan and placing it by its hash fails with `not_ready_or_absent` (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`).

A repeated placement returns it and writes nothing (P-06).

Continuity: The same placement is returned after the source file has left the folder
(`test_placing_again_returns_the_same_result_without_writing`).
open_points.question: Does conflict-copy exclusion override replay of an existing placement, or must a repeated placement still return the existing M04 record when the requested hash is now present only under a conflict-copy name?
options: Return the existing placement because replay does not place the current file.
Fail with `not_ready_or_absent` because the current source is a conflict copy.
Return an existing placement only when no conflict-copy file with that hash is present.
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing placement without reading or placing the conflict copy.

witness.initial: An ordinary file with hash H was placed, creating an M04 record; afterward the ordinary path disappears and a Syncthing conflict-copy path with the same bytes and hash H remains.
events: The calling flow requests placement for project P and hash H again.
outcomes: M04 and P-06 return the existing placement and write nothing.
INV-18's Required tests wording requires placement by the conflict copy's hash to fail with `not_ready_or_absent`.
witness.observer: The calling flow receives either the existing placement or an error.

open_points.subject: A1 — concurrent rename and placement
open_points.text: INV-18: a Syncthing conflict copy is neither reported by a scan nor placed.
open_points.question: At what point during placement is the conflict-name condition evaluated, and what is the required result if a ready ordinary file is renamed to a conflict-copy name while placement is in progress?
options: Classify the path once before opening it.
Recheck the path immediately before committing the placement.
Hold a stable file handle and classify the name captured when the operation began.
Define a linearization point that decides whether the file counts as ordinary or conflicting.
open_points.default_guess: Recheck eligibility immediately before committing the placement and refuse if the current path is ignored.

witness.initial: A scan reported `photo.jpg` as ready with hash H.
events: The calling flow starts placement of H.
After placement finds or opens the file but before it commits, Syncthing renames it to `photo.sync-conflict-20261118-device.jpg`.
outcomes: Placement uses the eligibility observed when it opened the ordinary file and succeeds.
Placement rechecks the current name, treats it as a conflict copy, and fails with `not_ready_or_absent`.
witness.observer: The calling flow sees success or refusal, and the owner may see a stored image created from a now-ignored path.

open_points.subject: R0-14 and A1 — effect of renaming
open_points.text:
The file stays in the folder, and the owner who wants that
version renames it, after which it is an ordinary photo.
open_points.question: What rename makes a conflict copy an ordinary photo: any rename, or only a rename whose resulting path no longer satisfies any ignored-name rule?
options: It becomes ordinary only when every path component no longer matches an ignored-name condition.
Only removal of the `.sync-conflict-` marker is required, even if another ignored-name condition remains.
open_points.default_guess: Require the resulting path to satisfy none of A1's ignored-name conditions.

events: The owner renames it to `PHOTO.SYNC-CONFLICT-20261118-DEVICE.JPG`, changing only letter case.
outcomes: R0-14's unqualified rename makes it an ordinary photo and it is offered.
A1's case-insensitive rule continues to ignore it.
witness.observer: The owner either sees the renamed photo in the next scan or does not.

open_points.subject: A1 — Syncthing conflict marker
open_points.text:
A name is ignored, in any letter case and at every level of the path, when it begins with a dot or
with `~syncthing~`, ends in `.tmp` or `~`, or contains `.sync-conflict-`, the mark of a Syncthing
conflict copy (R0-14).
open_points.rule:
У значения, которое читает генерируемый код, ровно три пути; путь
выбирается по тому, что это за значение, и у значения один дом (§15.4).

open_points.question: The `.sync-conflict-` marker and the other code-read ignored-name policy values must be placed in a provider constant and named to generated code as the imported constant, or remain design facts outside the specification instead of being supplied as literals.
